title: Flow frame - five bugs that hit EVERY flow: inputs lost on navigation, spacebar jumps a stage, no arrow-key nav, colour picker closes the overlay, promptRequired enforced nowhere
description: Fabio, 2026-08-23, from the first live look at the Scribble to Object flow (MPI-567). All four are in SHARED flow-frame code, not in any one flow, so they were split out of MPI-567 to run in parallel. Root causes are already traced - see plan.md, do not re-derive. (1) INPUTS ARE LOST ON NAVIGATION: state.s_flowInputs is written in exactly ONE place, inside _run (MpiBaseFlow.js ~2038), so anything dropped or typed before pressing Generate is never persisted; the shell destroys MpiBaseFlow on navigation (MPI-345) and the reopen seeds from {}. Drop a photo, visit the gallery, come back - it is gone. (2) SPACEBAR JUMPS A STAGE: the prev/next arrows are real <button>s (MpiBaseFlow.js ~248) that keep focus after a click, so spacebar is NATIVE button activation - nobody wrote a handler. Fabio: this cannot happen. (3) ARROW KEYS SHOULD NAVIGATE: left/right = previous/next step. Deliberately absent today (MpiBaseFlow.js ~1342 says so and gives two reasons); Fabio's call overrides that comment, so heal it rather than leaving it contradicting the code. (4) THE COLOUR PICKER CLOSES THE WHOLE FLOW: MpiColorPicker.openPopup emits a BARE ui:close-all-popups (MpiColorPicker.js:208); MpiOverlay:234 exempts only {reason:'overlay-open'}, so the picker takes the full-page overlay down with it and the user lands back on the gallery. Shared Primitive with 6 consumers - sweep them all. (5) promptRequired IS DECLARED 15+ TIMES AND ENFORCED NOWHERE: commandRegistry.js sets promptRequired on fifteen-odd ops and its own JSDoc calls a prompt mandatory, but grepping js/ finds no consumer at all - so Fabio ran Scribble to Object with an EMPTY prompt and got a shape invented from the ControlNet hint. The frame's empty-run guard (MpiBaseFlow ~2029) only fires when there is NEITHER media NOR a prompt. Found while wiring MPI-567's prompt and handed here because the fix is frame code. Either honour the flag or delete it from all fifteen ops - a declaration that lies is worse than none. MPI-567 is running IN PARALLEL and owns js/data/flowsRegistry.js, commandRegistry.js, operationRegistry.js, operation_registry.json, universal_workflows.js, modelRegistry.js, MpiFlowLibrary.js, the two flow_scribble_object.json copies and tests/flow-model-choice.test.cjs. Do NOT edit those. This card owns the frame and the Primitive.
acceptance: A flow input survives leaving the flow and coming back, WITHOUT a run: drop a photo, go to the gallery, reopen the flow, the photo is still in its slot
The persistence fix is at the ROOT - inputs are persisted when they CHANGE, not only at _run - and it is verified on a second flow as well as Scribble to Object
Spacebar no longer advances a step from any surface in a flow, including immediately after clicking a nav arrow
ArrowLeft / ArrowRight move to the previous / next step, through Hotkeys.bind with real hotkeyRegistry ids - never a raw window keydown listener
Arrow-key nav does not fight a gizmo: it is inert while the user is typing in a field, and it does not steal a drag from the box or paint gizmo
The MpiBaseFlow.js ~1342 comment claiming there is deliberately no arrow-key hotkey is healed, not left contradicting the code
Opening MpiColorPicker inside a Flow overlay leaves the overlay OPEN - the picker no longer emits a bare ui:close-all-popups
All six MpiColorPicker consumers are checked, not just the flow one: MpiStepPaint, MpiToolOptionsCrop, MpiToolOptionsMaskAdjust, MpiToolOptionsPaint, MpiToolOptionsRemoveBg, MpiToolOptionsResize

promptRequired is either HONOURED (a flow whose op declares it refuses to run on an empty prompt, with a ui:warning and no gen fired) or DELETED from all the ops that declare it - the chosen scope stated explicitly, never left inert
No file owned by MPI-567 is edited (see description) - if the fix genuinely needs one, file an mpi-message and stop that line of work
npm test passes, and each fix has a test or a stated reason why it cannot have one
